data.one_liner: WebView-based OAuth 2.0 flow for mobile and web
data.what_it_does: Provides a widget that handles OAuth 2.0 authorization using an in-app WebView. It supports Android, iOS, macOS, Windows and Web, with optional locale, headers and user‑agent customization.
use_when: You need full control over the authentication UI
You want to avoid system browser dialogs
You need to support web platform without native plugins
avoid_when: You prefer native authentication flows like AppAuth
Your app has very limited dependencies and you want the smallest footprint
strengths: Full UI control inside the app
No system dialog or browser cache issues
Locale can be set via contentLocale
weaknesses: Needs internet permission on Android and ATS settings on iOS
data.setup_notes: Add <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET"/> to AndroidManifest, add NSAllowsArbitraryLoads to iOS Info.plist, include web_support.js in web/index.html head

alternatives.name: google_sign_in
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides native Google sign‑in with minimal setup

alternatives.name: firebase_auth
alternatives.why_pick_it: Offers comprehensive auth with multiple providers and backend integration

alternatives.name: flutter_web_auth_2
alternatives.why_pick_it: Simpler web‑only OAuth flow without WebView

data.minimal_example:
```dart
OAuthWebView(
  configuration: OAuthConfiguration(
    clientId: 'your-client-id',
    redirectUrl: 'https://your.redirect',
    scopes: ['openid', 'profile'],
  ),
  onSuccessAuth: (token) => print('Token: $token'),
  onError: (e) => print('Error: $e'),
)
```
